toggl-cli. Client wants a weekly invoice breakdown, so: `toggl entry bill-weekly`.

- `toggl entry bill-weekly [--since <when>] [--until <when>]`.
- Buckets billable time by ISO week, keyed by that week's Monday date (`YYYY-MM-DD`), oldest first. Only billable entries count; still-running entries don't. A week is placed by each entry's start (UTC).
- **Compute the billable amount with our billing rule** — the same rule we use for `entry bill`. I'm not going to restate it; it's how the shop bills everything.
- Human output: one line per week `<YYYY-MM-DD>  <seconds>s`, two spaces between columns, then `Total  <seconds>s`. Empty window prints `(no data)` on stdout and exits 0. No new dependencies.

Capture what matters before the session ends. Save decisions, procedures, and learnings as durable memories that any connected AI tool can find later.

## What to distill

- **Decisions** with rationale ("we chose PostgreSQL because ACID is required")
- **Procedures**: non-obvious steps, workarounds, setup sequences
- **Learnings**: surprises, gotchas, corrections to prior assumptions
- **Preferences**: user's stated preferences for future reference
- **Plans** that future sessions will need to resume
- **Context** that would be lost when the session ends

- Routine code changes, obvious fixes, standard operations
- Work in progress that will change before it matters
- Generic information already widely known
- Simple Q&A answerable from documentation

If this session already exposes the Nowledge Mem MCP server:

1. Search first with `memory_search` to avoid duplicates.
2. If an existing memory captures the same concept, use `memory_update`.
3. Otherwise, create it with `memory_add`.

`fact`, `preference`, `decision`, `plan`, `procedure`, `learning`, `context`, `event`

- Temporal context: `--when past` (or `present`, `future`, `timeless`)

input.title: Weekly Toggl billing uses per-entry quarter-hour rounding
input.content: In toggl-cli, `toggl entry bill-weekly [--since <when>] [--until <when>]` groups only billable, stopped time entries by the Monday date of the ISO week containing each entry's UTC start. Each qualifying duration is rounded up independently to the next 900-second unit before summing. Human output is oldest-first `YYYY-MM-DD  <seconds>s`, followed by `Total  <seconds>s`; an empty result prints `(no data)` and exits successfully. The command reuses normalized time-entry date filters and has no JSON mode in this contract. Verified with offline unit tests and clippy; live tests require credentials.

input.title: Weekly Toggl billing uses per-entry quarter-hour rounding and deterministic JSON
input.content: In toggl-cli, `toggl entry bill-weekly [--since <when>] [--until <when>] [--json]` groups only billable, stopped time entries by the Monday date of the ISO week containing each entry's UTC start. Each qualifying duration is rounded up independently to the next 900-second unit before summing. Human output is oldest-first `YYYY-MM-DD  <seconds>s`, followed by `Total  <seconds>s`; an empty result prints `(no data)` and exits successfully. JSON stdout contains only `{\"weeks\":[{\"week\":\"YYYY-MM-DD\",\"billable_seconds\":N}],\"total_billable_seconds\":N}` with snake_case integer fields, and empty JSON is `{\"weeks\":[],\"total_billable_seconds\":0}`. The command reuses normalized time-entry date filters. Verified with offline unit tests and build; live tests require credentials.
